security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel CoVE host driver passes a non-zero _hi address parameter to any CoVE-IO SBI function on RV64, violating the spec mandate that _hi must be zero on RV64; the TSM may compute a combined physical address with spurious high bits, redirecting IOMMU mappings, DMA descriptors, or IDE key material to unintended physical pages
security_spec.summary: CoVE-IO SBI address _lo/_hi split mandates _hi==0 on RV64; non-zero _hi in MMIO-map or IDE-key calls lets a buggy kernel driver redirect TSM-programmed IOMMU page tables to host memory, breaking TVM confidentiality

findings.finding: SBI STA extension properly passes hi=0 on RV64 (line 71: IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_32BIT) ? upper_32_bits(...) : 0). This is NOT a CoVE-IO SBI function but demonstrates the correct _hi-zeroing pattern that a CoVE-IO driver should follow.
findings.snippet:
unsigned long hi = IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_32BIT) ? upper_32_bits((u64)pa) : 0;
return sbi_sta_steal_time_set_shmem(lo, hi, 0);

findings.finding: KVM STA handler properly rejects non-zero shmem_phys_hi on RV64 with SBI_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS (line 108-109). Not a CoVE-IO function, but demonstrates correct defensive _hi checking.

KVM forwards all SBI calls in the experimental range (0x08000000-0x08FFFFFF) to userspace via KVM_EXIT_RISCV_SBI. If a guest OS or VMM invokes CoVE-IO FIDs through this path, raw guest register values (including potentially non-zero _hi on RV64) would be forwarded without the kernel validating that _hi==0.
